item_04_lesson_56_outcome_family_proxy.reasoning: Five family-adjacent paradigms directly test the mechanism 'funding rate extreme own-history statistic predicts forward directional return'. All five produced broad-falsified results. Paradigm 156 finding was decisive: 'BTC funding p90/p10 regime carries near-zero directional information for alts; funding is a LAGGING positioning marker, not a leading macro driver'. Paradigm 243 provided the mathematical proof: focus+mirror = -2*fee identity for EVERY (T,h) combination proves the transform contains zero directional info; long-drift baseline explains all observed asymmetry. Paradigm 250's percentile-rank transform is monotone-equivalent to a z-score/skewness/level transform for the purpose of 'detecting extreme own-history position' — the mechanism is identical to the falsified family, only the surface statistic differs. Per Lesson #56 amendment (paradigm 245 + 242 codification), a monotone-equivalent noise-reduction transform of a family-saturated substrate does NOT restore predictive content.

item_05_lesson_39_mathematical_mirror_an.reasoning: Paradigm 243 demonstrated that for per-sym funding own-history extreme x bilateral SNT, focus+mirror ALWAYS sums to exactly -16bp = -2*fee. This is a mathematical identity, not an empirical finding: when the same trigger cell is evaluated with SHORT vs LONG on the same forward-return realization, the two sides differ only by (-r-fee) vs (+r-fee), forcing sum = -2*fee. Paradigm 250 uses the same 4-quadrant SNT construction on the same substrate. The identity WILL hold. The only rescue would be if the percentile-rank trigger were to produce a materially different set of trigger events than the skewness trigger — but both are monotone functions of the same underlying funding distribution position, so trigger overlap is very high (>60% overlap in trigger dates per own-history extreme statistic family). Even if trigger sets differ, the mathematical identity applies within each set.
